countries.name: Albrenn
countries.currencyNote: Pounds and pence, just like home.
rules: No special food rules. Customers like chips with everything and a cup of tea after.
countries.entryText: Home turf. Everyone already knows your name here.

countries.name: Caledh
rules: No special food rules.
Locals are proud of their own fish and their own weather.
countries.entryText: A short hop north. The menu travels well, though the wind may blow your sign away.

countries.name: Velland
rules: No special food rules.
Strict about bread: if your buns are squashy, people will say so, loudly.
countries.entryText: Velmont loves its own chip shop, Maison Frites. You'll need to win people over one bun at a time.

countries.name: Ostria
rules: No special food rules.
Big appetite for breakfast: muffins and coffee sell well before work.
countries.entryText: Port Sarn wakes up early and hungry. A breakfast menu would make friends fast.

countries.name: Westrian Union
rules: No special food rules.
Portions are expected to be big, and drive-thru lanes are expected to be quick.
countries.entryText: The land of the drive-thru. Big Sky Burgers got here first, so you'll be the new kid in town.

countries.name: Nihara
rules: No special food rules.
Customers expect everything spotless, on time and the same every visit.
countries.entryText: Kaito rewards a tidy, standardised kitchen. Sometimes a brand becomes part of a local holiday, and nobody quite knows why.

countries.name: Isla Verde
rules: No special food rules.
Families love sweet flavours, fried chicken and long weekend lunches.
countries.entryText: Manara adores Jolly Hen, its very own chain. Beating a local hero is hard; joining the party with a local dish might work better.

countries.name: Saravan
rules: No beef: cows are respected and not eaten by many people here.
No pork either.
Lots of customers are vegetarian, so veggie options sell brilliantly.
countries.entryText: A beef burger menu won't work in Vasant. Swap to chicken and veggie buns, or localise the menu before you open.

countries.name: Al-Rimal
rules: Halal: no pork, and meat must come from halal-certified suppliers.
No alcohol on the menu.
countries.entryText: Qamar's kitchens are halal. Take bacon and sausage off, check your meat suppliers, and the city is yours to win.

countries.name: Tevah
rules: Kosher: no pork and no shellfish.
Meat and dairy are never served in the same dish, so no cheeseburgers.
Many places close on the day of rest each week.
countries.entryText: Seren keeps kosher. Your cheeseburger needs a rethink: the patty can stay, but the cheese has to go.

no-beef.name: No beef
no-beef.explain: Many people here don't eat beef. Any dish with a beef patty, mince or steak loses most of its customers until you localise the menu.

no-pork.name: No pork
no-pork.explain: Bacon, sausages and pork belly are off the table. Swap them for chicken or egg.

halal.name: Halal
halal.short: No pork, no alcohol, halal meat only.
halal.explain: Halal kitchens use meat from certified suppliers, never serve pork, and keep alcohol off the menu.

kosher.name: Kosher
kosher.short: No pork or shellfish; never meat with dairy.
kosher.explain: Kosher kitchens never serve pork or shellfish, and never put meat and dairy in the same dish. A cheeseburger breaks two rules at once!
